common_root_cause: All 12 artifacts claim state=SUCCESS at root but were emitted without the receipt_core condition-10 envelope fields the catalog's output_schema shims require (downstream_consumers on all 12; manifest_registration/residual_unknowns/evidence/min_bytes_threshold/artifacts on several), with artifacts[] rows missing bytes/sha256. Two artifacts additionally carry FAILED sentinels against their own SUCCESS state (RES-0157, RES-0164), and two carry OPEN P0/P1 defects inside a SUCCESS state (RES-0164 P0, RES-0160 P1). Probe content itself is live (all 24 probe reruns exit 0 with SUCCESS markers) and every primary artifact sha256 matches its UNIT-ARTIFACT-MANIFEST.json row under CRLF->LF normalization - the failure is envelope/schema validity, not probe liveness.
path_to_green: Builders must re-emit the 12 artifacts as receipt_core-conformant envelopes (add the missing condition-10 fields, resolve the two FAILED sentinels and two open P0/P1 defects at their source, then re-hash). After re-emission, a fresh independent review round re-runs this battery and, if green, closes the receipts to SUCCESS with reviewer.verdict=PASS + independent=true.
residual_unknowns: Whether the catalog output_schema assignment (logical artifact-class shims delegating to receipt_core) is the intended contract for these RES research artifacts, or whether the catalog rows themselves are mis-declared, is a program-level question for the orchestrator - it does not change this round's verdicts, which enforce the contract as declared.
RES-0158's content probes pass, but its evidence/8/probes payload is schema-malformed; whether the underlying measurement claims survive re-emission is not judged here.
